evidence.finding: Aggregate offered volume was 22.78% above forecast at 10:15 and 22.37% above forecast at 10:45.
The only below-target intervals were 10:15 and 10:45, exactly coinciding with the two largest post-onset demand peaks; service level was 75.00% and 77.42%.
ASA peaked at 48.73 seconds at 10:15 and 47.73 seconds at 10:45, contemporaneous with the demand peaks and service-level breaches.
At 10:15, General Service received 50 calls but answered 43; ASA reached 63.71 seconds and service level fell to 63.27% with staffing fixed at 19.
Service remained above target at 09:45 and 10:00, recovered to 84.52% between the two breaches, and recovered after 10:45; the impact was transient rather than continuously sustained.
Scheduled and logged-in staffing remained constant at 49 throughout the window, and queue staffing did not decline.
No routing-change or platform event was recorded.

primary_root_cause_detail: Transient post-onset demand spikes most likely caused the two actual below-target intervals. At 10:15 and 10:45, aggregate demand was more than 22% above forecast and coincided with peak ASA and service levels of 75.00% and 77.42%. General Service directly accumulated seven calls during the 10:15 spike. The degradation was recurrent but not continuous, and the 09:45 interval itself was above target.
recommended_actions: Use interval-level demand-over-forecast alerts to trigger temporary overflow coverage before service falls below target.
Review intraday capacity thresholds for General Service, particularly when offered volume approaches 50 calls per interval.
Monitor queue accumulation and ASA alongside service level to distinguish transient demand pressure from sustained incidents.
Align incident timestamps with the first verified below-target interval; in this case the first demonstrated breach was 10:15, not 09:45.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Although the post-onset mean remained above target, two separate intervals breached 80%; both coincided with demand and ASA peaks, and the 10:15 interval included directly observed queue accumulation.
Scheduled and logged-in staffing remained constant, with only a 0.77% reduction in mean productive staffing.
Aggregate AHT decreased after onset, and General Service AHT was normal during its severe 10:15 breach.
No routing event or material transfer-rate increase was observed.
No platform event occurred, and performance recovered between demand peaks.

stakeholder_summary: Two recurrent but noncontinuous service-level breaches occurred after the stated incident start. Both aligned with the largest above-forecast demand intervals and peak ASA; General Service also showed direct queue accumulation at 10:15. Transient demand pressure remains the most likely cause, with moderate confidence.
